title: Co-op: Thralls Leave With Their Necromancer
items: When a co-op partner leaves, their thralls now leave with them instead of staying behind in the host's world, fighting for nobody.

title: Co-op Joining Fixed
items: Joining a friend's session works again: the joiner now actually connects to the host instead of loading for a minute and failing with "The host did not answer".

title: Stairs, Fen and Loot Icons
items: Bag: a long set-bonus line no longer stretches the Reliquary, so the bag grid stays fully visible and the window stops jumping when you pick an item.
Depths stairs look like stone stairwells with steps again, instead of a flat circle.
The Mourning Fen hummocks are muted peat mounds with a pale rim, closer to how they used to look.
Loot on the ground now shows the item's own icon (helm, chest, staff...) instead of a plain square.
Clicking the minimap shows the amber destination marker again while your hero walks there.

title: Threading Options (experimental)
items: Settings → Graphics: two new opt-in switches to try on your PC, both off by default and applied after a restart: Physics on a separate thread (experimental) and Separate render thread (only with the Mobile renderer).
If the game crashes soon after you change one, it starts with all graphics options back to normal; starting with `--safe-graphics` does the same.
F3 and bug reports show which renderer and threading options are active.

title: Lighter on the Graphics Card
items: Graveyard and cathedral props draw in far fewer batches (about a third fewer draw calls in the Hollow Graves and the Nave).
Spell sparks and embers are now animated by the graphics card instead of the CPU, so heavy fights spend far less time on effects.
Enemies of the same kind share one material, so crowds switch rendering state much less.
Ultra uses the 8 nearest torches like High does (this renderer lights each object with at most 8 anyway).
Low and Medium show fewer effect particles at full saturation, to stay smooth on weaker machines.
New: Settings → Graphics → Renderer → Mobile (Vulkan, experimental). Try it if you like; if it fails to start, the game comes back in the normal renderer.
Auto resolution only lowers resolution when the graphics card is the bottleneck, so the picture no longer gets blurry for nothing.

title: Smoother and Faster
items: Bag: you can now drag gear from the Reliquary onto its matching character slot or tool-belt cell to equip it, and item icons keep their proportions instead of stretching.
Respawning no longer leaves your hero lying in the death pose.
Thralls animate smoothly again: anything on screen now animates every frame (they were updating at a fraction of the frame rate).
Movement of your hero, enemies, thralls and bosses is smoothed between simulation steps, so it looks fluid on 120/144 Hz screens.
Big fights cost less: enemies far from the action think less often, wave spawns are spread over a few frames, and corpses stop animating once they settle.
Textures use the GPU's compressed formats: about 75% less video memory with the same look.
Fewer shadows to draw in crowds (the nearest enemies keep theirs), and the HUD and minimap only redraw what changed.
Settings → Window mode: choose Windowed, Windowed borderless or Fullscreen.
Typing in a text field (like the bug report window) no longer moves your hero, whatever keys you have bound to movement.

title: Better Bug Reports
items: Settings → Report a bug can now attach the end of your game log, including the session that crashed if the game closed on you. It is ticked by default; untick it to leave the log out.
Before sending, your computer's user folder is hidden and anything that looks like a password or login token is blanked.
Fixes for reported bugs now show as "Fixed — live now" in your report list as soon as the update is out, and are announced in #deathmuffin.

title: One Game: the Baseline
items: Death Muffin is now one game: the Windows client from the launcher, played online. The browser version is retired.
Online is open to everyone. Sign in with your existing account; your online characters carry over.
Necromancer only for now: the four necromancer disciplines are playable. The other five are shown as Coming later while they are rebuilt properly.
A character on a discipline that is not playable yet can switch to a necromancer discipline.
Characters from the old offline edition are removed when you start the game online.
The launcher has one Play button: it downloads, updates and starts the game.
Behind the scenes: old code and documents cleared out and every test passing, so fixes and polish land faster from here.
